# roottrace

roottrace 计算数据批次的 Merkle 根值，用于比较两个批次的内容是否一致。

## 构建

```sh
cargo build --offline
```

## 测试

```sh
cargo test --offline
```

除单元测试（SHA-256 向量、记录划分、MTH 递归构造、包含证明逐位置验证）外，
`tests/root_regression.rs` 通过实际构建出的命令做端到端回归：以事先固定的完整
根值校验 7、8、9 条记录（跨过 8 条这一二次幂边界）三个共享前七条记录的固定批次，
并覆盖重复内容改一个位置、交换两条不同记录、遗漏空记录、重复纳入一条记录、
末尾 LF 有无等价，以及空文件与单个 LF 的区别；同时校验成功输出恰为一行 64 位
小写十六进制加换行、退出状态为 0、stderr 无失败信息，并保留 `--version`、
参数错误（退出 2）和读取失败（退出 1）的既有行为。

`tests/prove_regression.rs` 对 `roottrace prove` 做同样的端到端保障：固定证明
向量（9 条非二次幂批次的首条、重复内容位置和末条，8 条平衡批次中部，含 NUL/
CR/非 UTF-8 字节的 10 条长短混合批次中的长记录，以及单个 LF 的空路径）逐字节
校验输出的一行 JSON；证明中的 `root` 与 `root` 命令对同一文件的结果一致；
相同内容位于不同位置得到不同证明；末尾 LF 有无两种文件形式给出逐字节相同的
证明；序号越界（含空文件）退出 1 且标准输出为空；负数、非数字、超过 64 位
无符号整数范围、缺少或多余参数退出 2 并输出用法说明；读取失败退出 1 且不输出
残缺证明。

`tests/verify_regression.rs` 对 `roottrace verify` 做端到端保障：直接使用
`tests/reference/rfc6962_vectors.py` 固定的同一批证明常量，另外把每个固定批次
每个位置的真实 `prove` 输出交给 `verify`，覆盖与现有命令的逐字节互操作；成功
时标准输出恰为 `verified\n`、退出 0、标准错误为空。记录文件按**全部字节**
处理——零字节文件核验空记录成功，而追加结束用 LF、空格、CR 或 NUL 都改变
记录并核验失败；含 NUL/CR/非 UTF-8 字节且以非文本字节结尾的长记录原样参与。
证明允许字段重排与任意 JSON 空白；证明自带的 `tree_size`、`root` 与命令行
可信值不一致时核验失败（证明不能自证）；重复内容只按 `leaf_index` 声明的
位置核验；路径缺一个、多一个（含单记录树的非空路径）或调换顺序都失败。空文件、
非对象、必需字段缺失或重复、类型错误、前导零/指数/小数、超出 64 位无符号
范围、非小写或长度不对的十六进制、`tree_size` 为 0 或序号越界、对象后有
多余字节，均以“证明格式无效”退出 1 且标准输出为空。可信树大小（必须为
ASCII 十进制正整数且不超 64 位）或可信根值（恰为 64 位小写十六进制）不合法、
缺少或多余参数退出 2 并输出用法说明；两个输入文件读取失败退出 1。

`tests/verify_escape_regression.rs` 针对证明文件中 JSON 字符串转义的端到端
回归保障（证明经其他 JSON 工具重新保存后，字符可能变成等价的 `\uXXXX`
表示，这种表示变化必须与证明内容损坏明确区分）：必需字段名与
`root`/`audit_path` 中的哈希字符无论直接书写、用合法 `\uXXXX` 转义（转义中
的十六进制字母可大写）还是在一个字符串中混用，解读后的字段与哈希完全相同
时核验结果完全相同（退出 0，标准输出恰为 `verified\n`，标准错误为空）。
重复字段按解读后的名称判断——同一对象中 `root` 与把某个字母写成转义的同名
字段即使值相同也算重复，`tree_size`、`leaf_index`、`audit_path` 同样——一律
按证明格式无效处理（退出 1、标准输出为空、标准错误说明格式问题），不任选
一个值继续核验。非法转义、未写完的 `\uXXXX`、孤立或错误配对的 Unicode 代理
项、字符串内未转义的控制字节与非法 UTF-8 字节同为格式错误。合法转义不放宽
哈希内容限制：解读后出现大写哈希字符、非十六进制字符或长度不符仍是格式
错误；解读后合法但与可信根值不符则保持核验失败。记录文件仍按全部原始字节
参与核验（含 NUL/CR/非 UTF-8 字节的长记录对转义证明核验成功），`prove` 的
原样输出继续直接兼容。

`tests/inspect_regression.rs` 对 `roottrace inspect` 做端到端保障：成功时
标准输出恰为一行、只含 `tree_size`、`leaf_index`、`root` 三个字段的 JSON
加换行，退出 0、标准错误为空，且与真实 `prove` 证明中对应字段逐字节一致、
与 `root` 命令的根值相同；字段重排、任意 JSON 空白以及字段名/哈希字符的
等价 `\uXXXX` 转义显示完全相同的信息。证明格式合法但审计路径数量、顺序或
内容无法证明声明位置（路径过短、多记录树空路径、任意根值）时仍正常显示，
且输出绝不包含 `verified` 等核验成功措辞。完整格式判定与 `verify` 相同：
非对象、截断、对象后多余字节、任一必需字段（含不展示的 `audit_path`）
缺失、`audit_path` 内哈希长度不对/大写/类型错误/数组未结束、重复字段
（含经转义后重名）、类型错误、前导零/小数/指数/超 64 位范围的整数、
`tree_size` 为 0、序号越界，均以证明格式无效退出 1、标准输出为空；
`u64::MAX` 的大小与在范围内的最大序号保持完整 64 位含义。文件不存在或指向
目录退出 1 且标准错误说明读取原因；缺少或多余参数退出 2 并输出用法说明；
同时确认该命令不改变 `verify` 与 `--version` 的既有行为。含非 UTF-8 字节
证明路径的覆盖位于 `tests/non_utf8_paths.rs`。

`tests/long_record_regression.rs` 对**长记录**做同样的端到端保障：记录去掉 LF
分隔符后为 54、55、56、63、64、65 字节（叶子哈希输入 `0x00 || 记录` 相应为
55–57 与 64–66 字节，贴近或跨过 SHA-256 的 56 字节填充边界与 64 字节分块边界）
以及一条 135 字节（>128，叶子输入进入第三个分块）的记录，各自作为单条记录
构成批次时都必须匹配固定根值；每条长记录内部都含 NUL、CR 与非 UTF-8 字节且
以非文本字节结尾，覆盖内容在内部和末尾的字节保真。两条长记录（65 与 135
字节）各有仅改动末尾一个字节的变体，根值必须对应修改后的完整记录——只处理
记录前面部分的实现无法通过。另设一个由长短记录共同组成的 10 条固定批次
（RFC 6962 的 k=8 切分使长记录同时落在左右子树），并同样校验该批次末尾字节
变体，确认长记录在批次中与单条记录时遵守同一标准。所有长记录批次都同时以
"末尾有/无结束用 LF"两种文件形式校验，二者表示同一记录序列、根值相同。

`tests/multi_read_regression.rs` 对**跨多次读取的记录**做端到端保障：`root`
命令以固定 64 KiB 缓冲区分段读取文件，该批次含一条 140000 字节（>128 KiB）
的记录，其字节跨越多次连续读取，读取边界绝不能成为记录边界——长记录按完整
字节恰好参与一次，不被截断、重复计入或拆成多个位置。批次为 10 条记录
（非二次幂，RFC 6962 按 k=8 切分，长记录落在左子树、末尾短记录落在右子树），
同时包含空记录、两处相同内容与结尾短记录；长记录前半段、后半段与末尾各有
可区分内容的标记，内部保留 NUL、CR 与非 UTF-8 字节。一条填充记录把第 2、3
条记录的分隔 LF 恰好放在第一次读取的最后一个字节与第二次读取的第一个字节
（连续 LF 跨过读取边界），每条空记录仍各占一个位置。同一批次末尾有/无结束用
LF 时输出逐字节相同；长记录后半段仅改动一个非 LF 字节后记录数与顺序不变，
根值对应修改后批次的固定值且与原批次不同。预期根值由独立脚本
`tests/reference/rfc6962_multiread_vectors.py` 固定，与
`tests/multi_read_regression.rs` 中的确定性构造逐字节对应同一记录序列。

`tests/library_verify.rs` 把 roottrace 当作**库**来端到端检验：证明与可信根值由
实际构建出的 CLI（`prove`/`root`）产生，大树情形沿用与
`tests/verify_big_tree_regression.rs` 相同的固定常量，核验本身则全部通过
`roottrace::verify_membership` 在内存中完成。覆盖：CLI 证明在批次每个位置都能
经库核验成功，且返回的类型化结果携带来自证明的序号与调用方的可信树大小、
根值；格式无效、核验失败、可信树大小为零（调用参数无效）三类错误按类型
区分；记录字节保真（空记录、末尾 LF/CR/空格/NUL、非 UTF-8 字节）；字段重排、
空白与等价转义被接受而重复字段仍被拒绝；重复内容只按声明位置核验；2^63、
2^63+1、2^64-1 的树大小与超过 32 位的序号保持完整 64 位含义。

`tests/verify_big_tree_regression.rs` 对**大树**（树大小接近 64 位无符号整数上限）
的核验做端到端保障：树大小为 9223372036854775808（2^63，二次幂树）、
9223372036854775809（2^63+1，不均匀树）与 18446744073709551615（2^64-1，不均匀
树）的合法证明都必须核验成功——标准输出恰为 `verified\n`、退出 0、标准错误为空。
这样的批次无法真正物化，因此证明是合成的：固定一条目标记录（含 NUL 与非 UTF-8
字节），路径第 i 个哈希为 i 的 64 位小写十六进制表示，可信根值由
`tests/reference/rfc6962_vectors.py` 用两种结构不同的独立实现（递归下降与自顶向下
记录转向再自叶向根折叠）重算并互验后固定。覆盖每个树大小的首条、末条以及左右
子树交界两侧的位置，包括序号恰为 2^32-1 与 2^32 等超过 32 位范围的情形；可信树
大小与序号必须保持精确整数含义（差 1 即核验失败），不因高位存在而被截断、变负或
被当作较小批次。2^63+1 树的末条记录是右子树唯一叶子，路径恰为一个哈希（不均匀
树形，不复制末尾记录也不补空记录）。同一大树证明的路径少一个、多一个或改动一个
哈希，以及记录字节有任何改动，都核验失败（退出 1、标准输出为空、标准错误说明
核验失败，而非用法错误或异常终止）；记录与路径不变、仅把可信树大小换成另一个
合法数值（含证明自带大小之外的相邻值）同样失败。树大小为 2^64-1 时序号等于树
大小属于证明格式无效（退出 1、标准错误为"证明格式无效"），与合法位置上的核验
失败保持区分。

预期根值不来自被检查的功能：`tests/reference/rfc6962_vectors.py` 是独立的 Python
参考实现（标准库 `hashlib.sha256`，递归定义与栈折叠两种算法互验），运行后可
重新生成各固定记录序列（含上述全部长记录与长短混合批次）对应的根值常量供核对；
跨多次读取批次的固定根值由复用同一对互验算法的
`tests/reference/rfc6962_multiread_vectors.py` 独立生成。
该脚本对包含证明同样提供两种结构不同的算法（RFC 6962 第 2.1.1 节 PATH 的递归
定义，以及自根向叶下降、兄弟子树哈希改用栈折叠计算的写法），二者在每个固定序列
的每个位置上结果一致，再用独立的递归包含验证器把每条证明重新哈希回批次根值；
脚本末尾输出供 `tests/prove_regression.rs` 使用的固定证明常量。

## 用法

```sh
roottrace root <文件路径>            # 计算批次根值
roottrace prove <文件路径> <记录序号>  # 生成指定记录在整个批次中的成员证明
roottrace inspect <证明文件>          # 只查看证明自身声明的大小、序号与根值
roottrace verify <记录文件> <证明文件> <可信树大小> <可信根值>
                                     # 仅凭一条记录和证明核验其位置，无需完整批次
roottrace --version                  # 打印版本号
```

### `roottrace root <文件路径>`

读取文件中的全部记录，按 RFC 6962 第 2.1 节的 SHA-256 Merkle Tree Hash
计算根值，向标准输出写出一行 64 个小写十六进制字符（行末带换行），退出状态为 0：

```text
b137985ff484fb600db93107c77b0365c80d78f5b429ded0fd97361d077999eb
```

两个文件的根值相同，说明它们的记录序列完全相同；根值不同则内容有差异。

**记录如何划分：** 文件按原始字节读取，以 LF（`\n`，0x0a）分隔记录，分隔符
本身不属于记录。记录中的空格、制表符、CR（`\r`）以及非 UTF-8 字节都属于
记录内容，原样参与计算。文件换行方式会影响根值：使用 CRLF 换行的文件，每条
记录末尾会多出一个 `\r` 字节，与对应 LF 换行的文件根值不同。

**非 UTF-8 文件路径：** 在 Unix 等允许文件名字节不是合法 UTF-8 的系统上，
路径按用户在命令行传入的原始字节原样访问，无需重命名或额外指定编码；相对
路径与绝对路径同样适用。因此路径中出现例如 0xff 字节时，程序不会在读取
文件前异常退出，也不会误读同目录下仅因显示替换字符“�”而看起来同名的另一个
文件。两个文件内容相同而路径字节不同，根值与证明完全相同。路径不存在、
指向目录或读取失败（即使路径本身含非 UTF-8 字节）时仍按下面的规则退出 1。
命令名、记录序号以及 `verify` 的可信树大小与可信根值参数必须是合法 UTF-8
文本；其中出现非 UTF-8 字节按用法错误退出 2。

**空文件与空记录的区别：**

- 空文件（0 字节）表示零条记录，根值是空输入的 SHA-256
  （`e3b0c442...b7852b855`）。
- 只含一个 LF 的文件表示一条空记录，与空文件的根值不同。
- 连续的 LF 会产生空记录，例如 `a\n\n` 是 `a` 和一条空记录。
- 末尾的 LF 只结束最后一条记录，不额外产生空记录，因此 `a\nb` 与 `a\nb\n`
  的根值相同。

重复内容不会被去重或合并：相同字节出现在不同位置仍是不同的记录，记录顺序
也参与计算。

**错误处理：**

- 缺少文件路径、参数多余或命令未知：向标准错误输出用法说明，退出状态为 2。
- 文件不存在、路径是目录或读取失败：向标准错误输出失败原因，退出状态为 1，
  标准输出不会写出任何根值。

### `roottrace prove <文件路径> <记录序号>`

为指定记录生成它在**整个批次**中的 RFC 6962 第 2.1.1 节包含证明（成员证明）。
记录划分规则与 `root` 完全一致（LF 分隔、末尾 LF 不增加记录、空记录占独立
位置、CR/NUL/非 UTF-8 字节原样保留）。

**记录序号（第二个参数）：** 从 0 开始的十进制非负整数，只接受 ASCII 数字，
按文件中的记录顺序定位：`0` 是第一条记录，`1` 是第二条，以此类推。相同内容
出现在多个位置时，证明的是序号指定的那个位置，不会去重，也不会自动改成第一
次出现的位置。序号等于或大于实际记录数时，该位置不存在。例如只含一个 LF 的
文件有一条记录，只能对序号 `0` 生成证明；真正的空文件（0 字节）没有任何可选
记录，对任何序号都报位置不存在。

成功时标准输出恰为一行 JSON 对象（行末带换行），退出状态为 0，标准错误为空：

```sh
$ printf 'a\nb\nc' > batch.txt
$ roottrace prove batch.txt 1
{"tree_size":3,"leaf_index":1,"root":"36642e73c2540ab121e3a6bf9545b0a24982cd830eb13d3cd19de3ce6c021ec1","audit_path":["022a6979e6dab7aa5ae4c3e5e45f7e977112a7e63593820dbec1ec738a24f93c","597fcb31282d34654c200d3418fca5705c648ebf326ec73d8ddef11841f876d8"]}
```

字段含义：

- `tree_size`：JSON 整数，完整批次的记录数。
- `leaf_index`：JSON 整数，被证明记录的序号（即命令行给出的位置）。
- `root`：64 位小写十六进制字符串，与 `roottrace root` 对同一文件输出的
  根值完全相同。
- `audit_path`：字符串数组，每个元素是 64 位小写十六进制哈希，按**从叶子向根**
  的顺序排列（RFC 6962 第 2.1.1 节的成员证明定义）。批次只有一条记录时为空
  数组 `[]`；记录数不是二次幂时按 RFC 的不均匀子树构造证明，既不复制末尾
  记录也不补空记录（例如 9 条记录时最后一条的证明只有一个哈希，即前 8 条
  子树的 MTH）。

证明中**不包含**原始记录：接收方用目标记录的原始字节、`leaf_index`、
`tree_size` 和 `audit_path` 重新哈希并与 `root` 比对，即可核对该记录确实位于
该位置。

**错误处理：**

- 位置不存在（空文件，或序号达到/超过实际记录数）：向标准错误说明该位置
  不存在，退出状态为 1，标准输出为空。
- 序号不是由 ASCII 数字组成的十进制非负整数（负数、非数字、超出 64 位无符号
  整数范围等），或缺少、多余参数：向标准错误输出用法说明，退出状态为 2。
- 文件不存在、路径是目录或读取失败：向标准错误输出失败原因，退出状态为 1，
  标准输出不会写出残缺证明。

### `roottrace inspect <证明文件>`

只查看一份成员证明**自身声明**的内容：批次大小、记录位置和根值。调用者
**不需要**准备目标记录，也**不需要**独立确认的可信树大小和可信根值——这个
操作不做成员核验。它适合在拿到一份证明、还没决定如何核验时快速读出其中的
三个关键信息。

成功时标准输出恰为一行 JSON 对象（行末带换行），**只包含** `tree_size`、
`leaf_index`、`root` 三个字段（整数不打引号，`root` 为 64 个小写十六进制
字符），退出状态为 0，标准错误为空。它直接接受 `prove` 的原样输出：

```sh
$ roottrace prove batch.txt 1 > proof.json
$ roottrace inspect proof.json
{"tree_size":3,"leaf_index":1,"root":"36642e73c2540ab121e3a6bf9545b0a24982cd830eb13d3cd19de3ce6c021ec1"}
```

输出中**没有** `audit_path`（它只被解读、不被展示），也绝不出现
`verified` 或其他表示核验成功的文字。

**显示的值来自证明自身，不能据此信任它们（重要）：**

- 一次成功的 `inspect` 只表示这份证明符合当前的文件格式，**不代表**证明里
  声明的记录已被证明属于该批次。哈希写法合法、但审计路径的哈希数量、顺序或
  内容根本无法把记录结合到声明位置时，`inspect` 仍然照常显示这三个值——
  因为这里既没有目标记录可重算，也没有独立可信值可比对。
- 因此显示出的 `tree_size` 与 `root` **不能**直接拿去当作 `verify` 的可信
  树大小和可信根值：证明可能来自不可信一方，用证明自带的值去核验同一份证明
  等于让证明自我背书。核验成员身份时，可信值仍须来自签名公告、带外账本，或
  对完整批次自行运行 `roottrace root` 等独立渠道，然后使用 `verify`。

```sh
# 下面的做法是错误的：把 inspect 显示的大小和根值当作可信输入，
# 同一份证明会"自我证明"。可信值必须独立获得。
roottrace verify record.bin proof.json 3 36642e73c2540ab121e3a6bf9545b0a24982cd830eb13d3cd19de3ce6c021ec1
```

证明的格式判定与 `verify` **完全相同**，不能只找到三个待显示字段就算成功：
字段重排、合法 JSON 空白（空格、制表符、CR、LF）以及字段名或哈希字符的等价
`\uXXXX` Unicode 转义不改变显示的信息；但证明必须是一个完整的 JSON 对象，
四个必需字段（含不展示的 `audit_path`）齐全且无重复，类型、整数与哈希合法，
`tree_size` 为正，`leaf_index` 在声明范围内。即使损坏位于 `audit_path`
中（例如某个哈希长度不对、数组没有结束），也按证明格式无效拒绝。解读后
重名的字段、`tree_size` 为 0、序号达到或超过声明大小同样拒绝。序号仍从
0 开始；大小和序号保留完整的 64 位无符号整数含义（即使该树无法真正物化，
只要字段在范围内就能显示）。

**错误处理：**

- 证明文件不存在、路径是目录或读取失败：标准输出为空，向标准错误说明读取
  原因，退出状态为 1。路径继续支持系统允许的非 UTF-8 字节，按命令行传入的
  原始字节访问。
- 证明格式无效：标准输出为空，向标准错误说明格式问题，退出状态为 1（与
  `verify` 对同类证明的判定和措辞一致）。
- 缺少或多余参数、命令未知：向标准错误输出用法说明，退出状态为 2。

### `roottrace verify <记录文件> <证明文件> <可信树大小> <可信根值>`

核验 `prove` 生成的包含证明：接收方**不需要完整批次**，只需目标记录本身、
证明，以及独立确认的树大小和根值，就能按 RFC 6962 第 2.1.1 节核对该记录确实
位于证明声明的位置。证明中的 `tree_size`、`root` 必须与命令行给出的可信值
逐字节一致——程序**不会**用证明自带的这两个字段作为信任依据，一份自洽但锚定
到别的树的证明无法通过核验。

**记录文件与批次文件的区别（重要）：**

- `root`/`prove` 的**批次文件**按 LF 分隔多条记录，末尾 LF 只结束最后一条，
  不额外产生空记录；空文件表示零条记录。
- `verify` 的**记录文件**保存**一条**目标记录的原始字节：文件的全部字节就是
  记录内容，**不按 LF 切分**，也**不删除**末尾的换行、空格或 CR。NUL 和非
  UTF-8 字节同样原样参与哈希。
  - 零字节文件表示一条**空记录**，可匹配 `tree_size` 对应树中的相应证明。
  - 若在记录后多写一个结束用 LF，记录内容就变成“原内容 + LF”，必须**核验
    失败**（批次文件里末尾 LF 不算内容；记录文件里每个字节都算）。
  - 从批次中取出记录交给 `verify` 时，应去掉分隔记录的那个 LF，只保留记录
    自身字节。

**可信树大小（第三个参数）：** ASCII 十进制**正整数**（只含数字，无符号、
空白或小数点），值不超过 64 位无符号整数范围；`0` 不接受（不存在包含记录的
零节点树）。

**可信根值（第四个参数）：** 恰好 64 个小写十六进制字符（32 字节），与
`roottrace root` 的输出格式一致。

**可信值从哪里来：** 必须由你**独立确认**，例如来自可信发布渠道（签名公告、
带外账本、对完整批次单独运行 `roottrace root` 等）。证明本身可能来自不可信
一方，所以其中的 `tree_size`/`root` 只用于和你的可信值比对，绝不能替代它们。

成功时标准输出**仅**为 `verified` 加换行，退出状态为 0，标准错误为空：

```sh
$ roottrace verify record.bin proof.json 9 a8a3e76ecf28b850e84cb5465729921212ffd07de3c0e6e170cd233bf723adc3
verified
```

核验流程：

1. 证明的 `tree_size` 必须等于可信树大小；
2. 证明的 `root` 必须等于可信根值；
3. `leaf_index` 必须在树中存在（`0 <= leaf_index < tree_size`）；
4. 从 `SHA-256(0x00 || 记录文件全部字节)` 出发，按证明 `audit_path` 的**原
   顺序**结合（非二次幂批次沿用 RFC 的不均匀树形，既不补记录也不复制末尾
   记录），结合方式由树大小与序号决定；单条记录（`tree_size` 为 1、序号 0）
   的路径必须为空数组 `[]`。
5. 重新算出的根必须等于可信根值。

路径少一个或多一个哈希（含单记录树却带了哈希）、顺序错误，或记录字节、
可信值、位置有任何不匹配，都不能成功。相同内容出现在多个位置时，只按证明
声明的 `leaf_index` 核验，不会搜索其他位置。

证明文件必须是**一个完整的 JSON 对象**，允许字段顺序和空白（空格、制表符、
CR、LF）变化。出现下列任一情况都判定为证明格式无效：不是 JSON 对象；必需字段
缺失或重复；值的类型错误（如整数写成字符串、`root` 不是字符串、
`audit_path` 不是数组）；`tree_size` 或 `leaf_index` 不是规范的 64 位无符号
JSON 整数（负数、小数、指数、前导零、超范围如 `1e400` 等都不行）；`root` 或
路径元素不是 64 位小写十六进制字符串；`tree_size` 为 0；`leaf_index` 越界；
对象之外还有多余字节。

**错误处理：**

- 内容、可信值或路径不匹配（核验失败），或证明格式无效：标准输出为空，向
  标准错误说明原因（分别提示核验失败/证明格式无效），退出状态为 1。
- 文件不存在、路径是目录或读取失败（记录文件或证明文件任一）：向标准错误
  说明原因，退出状态为 1，标准输出为空。路径继续支持系统允许的非 UTF-8 字节，
  按命令行传入的原始字节访问。
- 缺少或多余参数、可信树大小不是 ASCII 十进制正整数或超出 64 位范围、可信
  根值格式不符：向标准错误输出用法说明，退出状态为 2。

### `roottrace --version`

```text
roottrace 0.1.0
```

## 作为 Rust 库调用

除命令行外，roottrace 同时是一个 Rust 库：其他 Rust 程序可以直接在内存中
核验成员证明，无需准备完整批次或临时文件。在 `Cargo.toml` 中把本包加入
`[dependencies]` 后，成员核验的入口是 `roottrace::verify_membership`。

下面用一个**含重复记录的小批次**给出可以整段复制的完整示例：记录、证明、
可信值全部作为常量硬编码在程序里，复制后即可编译运行并得到真实的核验结果，
不需要先准备任何输入文件。

### 固定输入：一个 4 条记录的批次

批次文件的全部字节是 `alpha\nbeta\nalpha\ngamma\n`（23 字节，末尾 LF 只
结束最后一条记录）。按 LF 分隔出的完整记录序列为：

| 序号 | 记录字节 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `alpha`（5 字节） | 与位置 2 的内容完全相同 |
| 1 | `beta`（4 字节） | |
| 2 | `alpha`（5 字节） | **目标位置**：要核验的记录在这里 |
| 3 | `gamma`（5 字节） | |

目标记录是序号 **2** 的 `alpha`。序号从 0 开始；位置 0 虽然与它字节完全
相同，但是树中的另一个位置，对应另一份证明，本次核验不涉及它。

对该文件运行命令行可以直接得到证明与根值，输出逐字节如下：

```sh
$ printf 'alpha\nbeta\nalpha\ngamma\n' > batch.txt
$ roottrace root batch.txt
e63979768f9a2e746fa65d9bc2b3c0c97346fa29188b7346912c9a462b0a4b56
$ roottrace prove batch.txt 2
{"tree_size":4,"leaf_index":2,"root":"e63979768f9a2e746fa65d9bc2b3c0c97346fa29188b7346912c9a462b0a4b56","audit_path":["4c79d0d62f7cf5ca8874155f2d3b875f2625da2bb3abc86bbd6833f25ba90e51","983cb57c04cddd52634edab38a7bef85708a974f114bbd9aa9ec5d4ce6656b4b"]}
```

- **证明**就是上面 `prove` 输出的那一整行 JSON（下面的程序以原始字节常量
  给出，与命令行输出逐字节兼容）。两个审计路径哈希按从叶向根的顺序，依次
  是同层兄弟叶子 `SHA-256(0x00 || "gamma")` 与左半边两棵叶子的父节点
  `MTH(["alpha","beta"])`。
- **可信树大小 4 与可信根值不是从证明里读出来的**，而是用证明之外的完整
  批次数据独立确认的：这里是对同一个批次文件**单独运行 `roottrace root`**
  得到的结果；在真实场景中可换成签名公告或带外账本。下面程序把这 64 个
  十六进制字符写成完整的 32 字节数组，逐字节给满、没有省略。证明里的
  `tree_size`/`root` 只用于和它们比对。

> **字节边界。** 库函数收到的 `record: &[u8]` 是**一条记录的全部内容**：
> 不按 LF 拆分，也不自动删除末尾的换行。从批次文件取出一条记录时，分隔它
> 的那个 LF **不包含**在内——本例的记录就是 5 个字节 `alpha`，不是
> `alpha\n`。因此额外给记录追加一个 LF，记录就变成 6 个字节的另一条记录。
> 另外，空切片 `b""` 表示**一条空记录**（对应只含一个 LF 的批次里的那一条），
> 它与“空树”是两回事：空树没有任何位置，可信树大小为 0 不能用来核验成员。

### 完整程序与实际结果

```rust
use roottrace::{inspect_proof, verify_membership, VerifyError};

fn hex(root: &[u8; 32]) -> String {
    root.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

/// 核验一条记录并按“结果类型”报告：成功就读出序号、树大小和根值；失败只
/// 区分错误变体。变体里附带的原因字符串仅供写日志，不要匹配它的固定文字。
fn check(label: &str, record: &[u8], proof: &[u8], trusted_size: u64, trusted_root: &[u8; 32]) {
    print!("{label}: ");
    match verify_membership(record, proof, trusted_size, trusted_root) {
        Ok(membership) => println!(
            "核验成功：位置 {}，树大小 {}，根值 {}",
            membership.leaf_index(),
            membership.tree_size(),
            hex(membership.root()),
        ),
        Err(VerifyError::MalformedProof(_)) => println!("MalformedProof（证明不符合完整格式）"),
        Err(VerifyError::VerificationFailed(_)) => println!("VerificationFailed（格式合法但不匹配）"),
        Err(VerifyError::InvalidTrustedSize) => println!("InvalidTrustedSize（可信树大小为零）"),
    }
}

fn main() {
    // 批次文件 alpha\nbeta\nalpha\ngamma\n 的完整记录序列（LF 分隔记录，
    // 末尾 LF 只结束最后一条，不属于任何记录）：
    //   位置 0 = "alpha"
    //   位置 1 = "beta"
    //   位置 2 = "alpha"   <- 目标记录；与位置 0 的字节完全相同
    //   位置 3 = "gamma"
    let record: &[u8] = b"alpha";

    // `roottrace prove <批次文件> 2` 的原样输出：完整 JSON，没有任何省略。
    let proof: &[u8] = br#"{"tree_size":4,"leaf_index":2,"root":"e63979768f9a2e746fa65d9bc2b3c0c97346fa29188b7346912c9a462b0a4b56","audit_path":["4c79d0d62f7cf5ca8874155f2d3b875f2625da2bb3abc86bbd6833f25ba90e51","983cb57c04cddd52634edab38a7bef85708a974f114bbd9aa9ec5d4ce6656b4b"]}"#;

    // 可信值独立于证明获得：对上面的“完整批次”运行 `roottrace root`
    // （生产中也可以来自签名公告或带外账本）。批次有 4 条记录，根值是
    // 下面这 32 个字节，逐字节对应上面的证明，但不是从证明里照抄的。
    let trusted_tree_size: u64 = 4;
    let trusted_root: [u8; 32] = [
        0xe6, 0x39, 0x79, 0x76, 0x8f, 0x9a, 0x2e, 0x74,
        0x6f, 0xa6, 0x5d, 0x9b, 0xc2, 0xb3, 0xc0, 0xc9,
        0x73, 0x46, 0xfa, 0x29, 0x18, 0x8b, 0x73, 0x46,
        0x91, 0x2c, 0x9a, 0x46, 0x2b, 0x0a, 0x4b, 0x56,
    ];

    // 1) 原记录 + 原证明 + 独立可信值：核验成功。
    check("原记录", record, proof, trusted_tree_size, &trusted_root);

    // 2) 记录末尾追加一个 LF，证明和可信值都不变：这是另一条记录，必失败。
    let mut with_lf = record.to_vec();
    with_lf.push(b'\n');
    check("加 LF", &with_lf, proof, trusted_tree_size, &trusted_root);

    // 3) 证明被截断（数组和对象都没结束）：不符合完整格式。
    check("截断证明", record, &proof[..proof.len() - 3], trusted_tree_size, &trusted_root);

    // 4) 可信树大小传 0：调用参数无效；这与“空记录”无关。
    check("大小为零", record, proof, 0, &trusted_root);

    // 5) inspect_proof 只读出证明自己的声明，完全不核验成员身份。
    let claims = inspect_proof(proof).expect("这份证明格式合法");
    println!(
        "inspect：证明自称 位置 {}、树大小 {}、根值 {}（未核验，不能当可信输入）",
        claims.leaf_index(),
        claims.tree_size(),
        hex(claims.root()),
    );

    // 6) 空切片表示一条空记录。下面是“只含一个 LF 的批次”（一条空记录、
    //    树大小 1、审计路径为空）的真实证明与独立根值。
    let empty_proof: &[u8] = br#"{"tree_size":1,"leaf_index":0,"root":"6e340b9cffb37a989ca544e6bb780a2c78901d3fb33738768511a30617afa01d","audit_path":[]}"#;
    let empty_root: [u8; 32] = [
        0x6e, 0x34, 0x0b, 0x9c, 0xff, 0xb3, 0x7a, 0x98,
        0x9c, 0xa5, 0x44, 0xe6, 0xbb, 0x78, 0x0a, 0x2c,
        0x78, 0x90, 0x1d, 0x3f, 0xb3, 0x37, 0x38, 0x76,
        0x85, 0x11, 0xa3, 0x06, 0x17, 0xaf, 0xa0, 0x1d,
    ];
    let m = verify_membership(b"", empty_proof, 1, &empty_root).expect("空记录应核验成功");
    println!("空记录：位置 {}，树大小 {}", m.leaf_index(), m.tree_size());
}
```

实际运行结果如下，每一行对应程序中的一次调用：

```text
原记录: 核验成功：位置 2，树大小 4，根值 e63979768f9a2e746fa65d9bc2b3c0c97346fa29188b7346912c9a462b0a4b56
加 LF: VerificationFailed（格式合法但不匹配）
截断证明: MalformedProof（证明不符合完整格式）
大小为零: InvalidTrustedSize（可信树大小为零）
inspect：证明自称 位置 2、树大小 4、根值 e63979768f9a2e746fa65d9bc2b3c0c97346fa29188b7346912c9a462b0a4b56（未核验，不能当可信输入）
空记录：位置 0，树大小 1
```

成功时从类型化结果 `Membership` 读取三个值：

- `leaf_index()` 返回 `2`——证明声明的、从 0 开始的记录序号。它只锚定
  位置 2；位置 0 那条同内容的 `alpha` **并不因此**被视为已核验（对它要
  另行用 `prove batch.txt 0` 生成的、`leaf_index` 为 0 的另一份证明）。
- `tree_size()` 返回 `4`——就是你传入的可信树大小（已与证明自带字段核对
  一致），不是从证明里另读出来的值。
- `root()` 返回那 32 个字节（`&[u8; 32]`）——就是你的可信根值，写成十六
  进制为 `e63979768f9a2e746fa65d9bc2b3c0c97346fa29188b7346912c9a462b0a4b56`，
  与 `roottrace root` 对该批次的输出逐字节相同。

“加 LF”一行演示字节边界的后果：只给目标记录末尾多追加一个 LF（记录变成
`alpha\n`），证明与可信值原封不动，结论就只能是核验失败，不会再出现成功
结果。

### 三类错误按类型区分，不要匹配原因字符串

处理 `Err(VerifyError)` 时要按**变体（类型）**分支决定怎么办；变体附带的
原因字符串只用于写日志，其文字可能调整，不要依赖它的固定措辞：

- `VerifyError::MalformedProof(reason)`：证明不符合**完整格式**——不是一个
  完整 JSON 对象、必需字段缺失或重复、值的类型错误、整数或哈希不合法、
  证明内 `tree_size` 为 0、序号越界、对象后有多余字节等。上例把证明末尾
  截掉 3 个字节即属此类。
- `VerifyError::VerificationFailed(reason)`：证明**格式合法**，但记录内容、
  可信树大小、可信根值或审计路径对不上。记录多一个 LF、可信值换成别的
  批次、证明自带大小/根值与可信值不一致、路径缺一个/多一个/顺序错，都归
  这一类。
- `VerifyError::InvalidTrustedSize`：调用参数无效——可信树大小为 0。该判断
  在解读证明**之前**完成，所以即便拿到的是一份内部 `tree_size` 为 0 的
  “证明”，报的也是这个类型而非格式错误。不存在包含记录的零节点树，它不是
  “空树中的成员证明”。

### `inspect_proof` 只读声明，其结果不能当可信输入

只想读证明自身的声明而不核验时，用
`roottrace::inspect_proof(&[u8]) -> Result<ProofClaims, InspectError>`：它用
与 `verify_membership` 完全相同的完整格式判定解读证明，成功则返回证明自称
的 `tree_size()`、`leaf_index()` 与 `root()`。但这一步**没有目标记录、没有
独立可信值，因此不做成员核验**——审计路径的哈希能否把记录结合到声明位置
完全不检查；只要格式合法，哪怕路径是随便填的，这些字段也会被原样读出。

所以一次成功的 `inspect_proof` 只表示“读出了证明自己的声明”。上例第 5 步
打印出的大小 4 与根值恰好和真值相同，仅仅因为这份证明确实是我们自己对真实
批次生成的；**绝不能**把 `claims.tree_size()`/`claims.root()` 直接回传给
`verify_membership` 去核验同一份证明——证明可能来自不可信一方，那样做等于
让证明自我背书。可信值仍须来自 `roottrace root`、签名公告或带外账本等
独立渠道。证明格式无效时返回 `InspectError::MalformedProof`；命令行的
`inspect` 子命令就建立在这个函数之上。

### 其他约定

库本身不向标准输出或标准错误打印任何内容；成功与失败如何展示完全由调用方
决定，失败时只返回上述错误，不会返回任何表示已核验成功的结果。命令行的
`verify` 子命令与库函数走完全相同的核验代码，两边对同一输入的结论一致。
树大小和序号始终保持完整的 64 位无符号整数含义，即使超过平台的指针宽度也
不会被截断。

lastPrompt: 为 roottrace 的成员证明生成功能补充长记录批次的回归保障。现有的大记录批次已经校验根值，也确认末条记录能够生成证明，但还没有完整约束这类批次的审计路径及实际核验结果。本次围绕一份十条记录的批次展开：序号 4 是一条 140000 字节的记录，内部及末尾含 NUL、CR 和非 UTF-8 字节，批次中仍有短记录、空记录和重复内容。长记录只占一个位置，全部字节参与证明，不能被截断、拆分或跳过…

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent reference vectors for the MULTI-READ root regression tests.

This script is NOT the program under test and does not execute roottrace.  It
computes the expected RFC 6962 section 2.1 SHA-256 Merkle Tree Hash roots for
a batch whose file is large enough that `roottrace root` (which streams the
file through a fixed 64 KiB read buffer) cannot see any whole record in one
read: one record is 140000 bytes (> 128 KiB) and spans several reads, and two
record-separating LFs land exactly on the last/first byte of a read boundary.

The roots are computed with the two structurally different, already
cross-validated reference algorithms from rfc6962_vectors.py (the RFC's
recursive definition and an order-sensitive stack fold over the standard
library `hashlib.sha256`); they must agree.  The Rust test
tests/multi_read_regression.rs rebuilds the exact same bytes with the same
deterministic construction and pins the printed constants, so the expected
roots are fixed independently of the implementation being checked.

Batch record sequence (10 records, a non-power-of-two count; RFC 6962 splits
k=8, so the long record at position 4 sits in the left subtree and the
trailing short record at position 9 in the right one):

    0  b"alpha"              short; duplicated byte-for-byte at position 6
    1  b""                   empty record
    2  PAD                   65528 bytes: b"pad:" + b"p" * 65524, placed so
                             its terminating LF is the LAST byte of the first
                             64 KiB read (file offset 65535)
    3  b""                   empty record; its LF is the FIRST byte of the
                             second read (offset 65536), so two consecutive
                             LFs straddle the read boundary
    4  LONG                  140000 bytes (> 128 KiB), spanning reads; NUL,
                             CR and non-UTF-8 bytes in both halves and at the
                             tail; distinct head/mid/tail markers
    5  b"beta\\r"            short, trailing CR is content
    6  b"alpha"              duplicate of position 0 (must not be merged)
    7  b""                   empty record
    8  b"\\xff\\x00z"        short, non-UTF-8 and NUL bytes
    9  b"end-record\\x01"    trailing short record, must reach the final root

Run:  python3 tests/reference/rfc6962_multiread_vectors.py
"""

import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from rfc6962_vectors import mth_fold, mth_recursive, split_records

READ_BUF = 64 * 1024  # the fixed read buffer `roottrace root` streams through

LONG_LEN = 140_000  # > 128 KiB: the record spans several consecutive reads
# Bytes before PAD: b"alpha\n" (6) + b"\n" (1) = 7.  PAD's terminating LF must
# land at offset READ_BUF - 1 (the last byte the first read returns).
PAD_LEN = READ_BUF - 1 - 7  # 65528
# Position of the single changed content byte inside LONG: in the second half
# of the record and (as a file offset) inside a later read than the record's
# first bytes.
MOD_POS = 100_000


def fill_byte(i: int) -> int:
    """Deterministic pseudo-random content byte; LF is remapped so the long
    record never contains its own separator.  Identical to the Rust
    `fill_byte` in tests/multi_read_regression.rs."""
    b = ((i * 2654435761) & 0xFFFFFFFF) >> 13 & 0xFF
    return 0x0B if b == 0x0A else b


def long_record() -> bytes:
    rec = bytearray(fill_byte(i) for i in range(LONG_LEN))
    rec[0:13] = b"MREAD\x00\xff\xfe\rHEAD"          # first-half marker
    mid = LONG_LEN // 2
    marker = b"\x00\xff\rSECOND-HALF"               # second-half marker
    rec[mid:mid + len(marker)] = marker
    tail = b"\x00TAIL\r\xff"                        # tail marker, non-text end
    rec[LONG_LEN - len(tail):] = tail
    return bytes(rec)


def long_record_m() -> bytes:
    """The same record with exactly ONE non-LF content byte changed, at
    MOD_POS in the second half; record length and every other byte kept."""
    rec = bytearray(LONG)
    old = rec[MOD_POS]
    rec[MOD_POS] = 0x41 if old != 0x41 else 0x42  # 'A' or 'B', never LF
    assert rec[MOD_POS] != old
    return bytes(rec)


PAD = b"pad:" + b"p" * (PAD_LEN - 4)
LONG = long_record()
LONG_M = long_record_m()

RECORDS = [
    b"alpha",
    b"",
    PAD,
    b"",
    LONG,
    b"beta\r",
    b"alpha",
    b"",
    b"\xff\x00z",
    b"end-record\x01",
]
RECORDS_M = [
    b"alpha",
    b"",
    PAD,
    b"",
    LONG_M,
    b"beta\r",
    b"alpha",
    b"",
    b"\xff\x00z",
    b"end-record\x01",
]


def join_lf(records, trailing=True):
    data = b"\n".join(records)
    if trailing and records:
        data += b"\n"
    return data


def root_of(records):
    a, b = mth_recursive(records), mth_fold(records)
    assert a == b, "reference algorithms disagree"
    return a.hex()


def describe(records):
    out = []
    for i, r in enumerate(records):
        if len(r) <= 32:
            out.append(f"    {i}: {len(r)} byte(s) {r!r}")
        else:
            out.append(f"    {i}: {len(r)} byte(s) {r[:16]!r} ... {r[-8:]!r}")
    return "\n".join(out)


def main():
    n = len(RECORDS)
    assert n == 10 and n & (n - 1) != 0, "record count must be a non-power of two"
    assert RECORDS[0] == RECORDS[6], "duplicate content at positions 0 and 6"
    assert RECORDS[1] == RECORDS[3] == RECORDS[7] == b"", "empty records"

    # Long-record shape: > 128 KiB, no LF anywhere, NUL/CR/non-UTF-8 in both
    # halves and at the tail, distinct markers in each region.
    half = LONG_LEN // 2
    assert LONG_LEN > 128 * 1024
    assert b"\n" not in LONG
    for region in (LONG[:half], LONG[half:]):
        assert 0x00 in region and 0x0D in region
        assert any(b >= 0x80 for b in region)
    assert LONG[:13] == b"MREAD\x00\xff\xfe\rHEAD"
    assert LONG[half:half + 14] == b"\x00\xff\rSECOND-HALF"
    assert LONG[-7:] == b"\x00TAIL\r\xff"

    # The one-byte modification: second half, non-LF, everything else equal.
    assert MOD_POS > half
    assert LONG_M != LONG and len(LONG_M) == len(LONG)
    diffs = [i for i in range(LONG_LEN) if LONG[i] != LONG_M[i]]
    assert diffs == [MOD_POS] and LONG_M[MOD_POS] != 0x0A

    # File layout: LFs at offsets 65535/65536 are consecutive and straddle
    # the 64 KiB read boundary; the long record spans several reads.
    data = join_lf(RECORDS)
    assert data[65535] == 0x0A and data[65536] == 0x0A
    assert data[65534] != 0x0A and data[65537] != 0x0A
    long_start = 7 + PAD_LEN + 1 + 1  # after PAD's LF and the empty record's LF
    long_end = long_start + LONG_LEN - 1
    assert long_start // READ_BUF < long_end // READ_BUF
    assert long_end // READ_BUF - long_start // READ_BUF >= 2, "must span >= 3 reads"
    assert split_records(data) == RECORDS
    assert split_records(join_lf(RECORDS, trailing=False)) == RECORDS

    root = root_of(RECORDS)
    root_m = root_of(RECORDS_M)
    assert root != root_m, "one content byte in the second half must matter"
    # Trailing-LF equivalence: both file forms encode the same sequence.
    assert split_records(data) == split_records(join_lf(RECORDS, trailing=False))

    print("# Generated by tests/reference/rfc6962_multiread_vectors.py")
    print("# Two independent RFC 6962 implementations agree for every vector.")
    print("#")
    print("# MREAD batch record sequence (10 records, non-power-of-two):")
    print(describe(RECORDS))
    print("#")
    print("# MREAD_M: identical except LONG[100000] changed")
    print(f"#   {LONG[MOD_POS]:#04x} -> {LONG_M[MOD_POS]:#04x} (second half of the long record)")
    print("#")
    print(f"# file bytes: {len(data)} (with trailing LF), "
          f"read buffer {READ_BUF}; long record at file offsets "
          f"{long_start}..{long_end} (reads {long_start // READ_BUF}..{long_end // READ_BUF});")
    print("# record-separating LFs at offsets 65535 and 65536 straddle the "
          "first read boundary")
    print()
    print(f"const ROOT_MREAD: &str = \"{root}\";")
    print(f"const ROOT_MREAD_M: &str = \"{root_m}\";")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Independent reference vectors for roottrace root-value regression tests.
3	
4	This script is NOT the program under test and does not execute roottrace.  It
5	computes RFC 6962 section 2.1 SHA-256 Merkle Tree Hash roots with two
6	independently written algorithms over the standard library `hashlib.sha256`:
7	
8	  * mth_recursive  - direct transcription of the RFC 6962 definition
9	                     (empty -> SHA-256(""); one leaf -> SHA-256(0x00||d);
10	                     n > 1 -> SHA-256(0x01 || MTH(0:k) || MTH(k:n)) with k the
11	                     largest power of two strictly smaller than n)
12	  * mth_fold       - order-sensitive left-to-right stack fold using the same
13	                     leaf/node prefixes (a structurally different computation
14	                     that must agree)
15	
16	It also computes RFC 6962 section 2.1.1 inclusion (audit) paths in two
17	structurally different ways:
18	
19	  * audit_path_recursive - direct transcription of the PATH definition
20	  * audit_path_fold      - the stack fold builds explicit subtree nodes with
21	                           intervals; the path is collected by walking from
22	                           the root down to the leaf's node
23	
24	A recursive RFC verifier (verify_inclusion) re-hashes every printed proof and
25	must arrive back at the batch root; proofs for duplicate content at another
26	position are additionally checked NOT to verify.
27	
28	A final section covers trees too large to materialise (sizes 2**63, 2**63+1
29	and 2**64-1): the audit path is built from deterministic synthetic sibling
30	hashes and the root an honest verifier must recompute is derived two
31	structurally different ways (recursive descent, and an iterative top-down
32	turn walk folded leaf-to-root), which must agree.
33	
34	Records are split exactly as roottrace documents: raw bytes on LF, the
35	separator excluded, a trailing LF only terminates the last record, and an
36	empty file holds zero records.
37	
38	Run:  python3 tests/reference/rfc6962_vectors.py
39	The printed constants are copied verbatim into tests/root_regression.rs and
40	tests/long_record_regression.rs.  Nothing here reads roottrace output, so the
41	expected roots are fixed independently of the implementation being checked.
42	"""
43	
44	import hashlib
45	
46	
47	def sha256(data: bytes) -> bytes:
48	    return hashlib.sha256(data).digest()
49	
50	
51	def mth_recursive(records):
52	    n = len(records)
53	    if n == 0:
54	        return sha256(b"")
55	    if n == 1:
56	        return sha256(b"\x00" + records[0])
57	    # Largest power of two strictly smaller than n.
58	    k = 1 << ((n - 1).bit_length() - 1)
59	    return sha256(b"\x01" + mth_recursive(records[:k]) + mth_recursive(records[k:]))
60	
61	
62	def mth_fold(records):
63	    # Iterative, structurally independent formulation: walk leaves left to
64	    # right, folding completed equal-height subtrees; a trailing uneven stack
65	    # is combined right-to-left.  Same RFC 6962 result, order sensitive.
66	    def node(left, right):
67	        return sha256(b"\x01" + left + right)
68	
69	    stack = []  # (height, hash)
70	    for r in records:
71	        h, height = sha256(b"\x00" + r), 0
72	        while stack and stack[-1][0] == height:
73	            _, lh = stack.pop()
74	            h, height = node(lh, h), height + 1
75	        stack.append((height, h))
76	    if not stack:
77	        return sha256(b"")
78	    root = stack[-1][1]
79	    for _, h in reversed(stack[:-1]):
80	        root = node(h, root)
81	    return root if stack else sha256(b"")
82	
83	
84	def split_records(data: bytes):
85	    if not data:
86	        return []
87	    records = data.split(b"\n")
88	    if data.endswith(b"\n"):
89	        records.pop()
90	    return records
91	
92	
93	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
94	# RFC 6962 section 2.1.1 inclusion (audit) paths.
95	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
96	
97	def audit_path_recursive(records, m):
98	    """Direct transcription of the PATH definition, leaf-to-root order.
99	
100	    PATH(m, [d0]) = []
101	    PATH(m, [d0..d(n-1)]) =
102	        PATH(m, d[0:k])       + [MTH(d[k:n])]   if m < k
103	        PATH(m - k, d[k:n])   + [MTH(d[0:k])]   if m >= k
104	    """
105	    n = len(records)
106	    if not 0 <= m < n:
107	        raise IndexError(f"index {m} out of range for {n} record(s)")
108	    if n == 1:
109	        return []
110	    k = 1 << ((n - 1).bit_length() - 1)
111	    if m < k:
112	        return audit_path_recursive(records[:k], m) + [mth_recursive(records[k:])]
113	    return audit_path_recursive(records[k:], m - k) + [mth_recursive(records[:k])]
114	
115	
116	def audit_path_fold(records, m):
117	    """Structurally different path producer: descend from the root to leaf m
118	    using the RFC split, computing each sibling subtree hash with the stack
119	    fold mth_fold (never mth_recursive), then reverse into leaf-to-root
120	    order. This shares no recursion structure with audit_path_recursive."""
121	    n = len(records)
122	    if not 0 <= m < n:
123	        raise IndexError(f"index {m} out of range for {n} record(s)")
124	    if n == 1:
125	        return []
126	    lo, hi = 0, n
127	    top_down = []
128	    while hi - lo > 1:
129	        size = hi - lo
130	        k = 1 << ((size - 1).bit_length() - 1)
131	        if m < lo + k:
132	            top_down.append(mth_fold(records[lo + k:hi]))
133	            hi = lo + k
134	        else:
135	            top_down.append(mth_fold(records[lo:lo + k]))
136	            lo = lo + k
137	    return list(reversed(top_down))
138	
139	
140	def verify_inclusion(leaf, m, n, path):
141	    """RFC 6962-bis recursive verifier: re-derive combination order from the
142	    tree geometry while consuming the supplied path. Returns the root."""
143	    def sub(mm, nn, pos):
144	        if nn == 1:
145	            return sha256(b"\x00" + leaf), pos
146	        k = 1 << ((nn - 1).bit_length() - 1)
147	        if mm < k:
148	            lh, pos = sub(mm, k, pos)
149	            rh = path[pos]
150	            pos += 1
151	        else:
152	            rh, pos = sub(mm - k, nn - k, pos)
153	            lh = path[pos]
154	            pos += 1
155	        return sha256(b"\x01" + lh + rh), pos
156	
157	    root, pos = sub(m, n, 0)
158	    assert pos == len(path), "proof length mismatch"
159	    return root
160	
161	
162	def root_of_file_bytes(data: bytes):
163	    recs = split_records(data)
164	    a, b = mth_recursive(recs), mth_fold(recs)
165	    assert a == b, "reference algorithms disagree"
166	    return a.hex(), recs
167	
168	
169	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
170	# Big-tree inclusion proofs: tree sizes 2**63, 2**63+1 and 2**64-1 sit at or
171	# above the signed/unsigned 64-bit boundary, so no batch file can ever be
172	# materialised for them. The proof is therefore synthetic: one fixed target
173	# record, and an audit path whose element i is the deterministic 32-byte
174	# value written as the 64-character lowercase hex of i (reproduced in Rust
175	# as format!("{i:064x}")). The trusted root is whatever an honest RFC 6962
176	# verifier recombines from (record, leaf_index, tree_size, audit_path); it is
177	# derived here by two structurally different computations that must agree.
178	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
179	
180	BIG_TREE_RECORD = b"big-tree-record\x00\xff\xfe"
181	
182	
183	def big_tree_path(depth):
184	    return [bytes.fromhex("%064x" % i) for i in range(depth)]
185	
186	
187	def big_tree_path_for(m, n):
188	    """The synthetic audit path for leaf m in a tree of n records: one
189	    element per level on the root-to-leaf descent."""
190	    depth = 0
191	    lo, hi = 0, n
192	    while hi - lo > 1:
193	        size = hi - lo
194	        k = 1 << ((size - 1).bit_length() - 1)
195	        if m < lo + k:
196	            hi = lo + k
197	        else:
198	            lo = lo + k
199	        depth += 1
200	    return big_tree_path(depth)
201	
202	
203	def big_root_recursive(record, m, n, path):
204	    """Direct transcription of the RFC 6962-bis recursive verifier: re-derive
205	    the combination order from the (uneven) subtree geometry while consuming
206	    the path in its given leaf-to-root order."""
207	    leaf = sha256(b"\x00" + record)
208	
209	    def sub(mm, nn, pos):
210	        if nn == 1:
211	            return leaf, pos
212	        k = 1 << ((nn - 1).bit_length() - 1)
213	        if mm < k:
214	            lh, pos = sub(mm, k, pos)
215	            rh = path[pos]
216	            pos += 1
217	        else:
218	            rh, pos = sub(mm - k, nn - k, pos)
219	            lh = path[pos]
220	            pos += 1
221	        return sha256(b"\x01" + lh + rh), pos
222	
223	    root, pos = sub(m, n, 0)
224	    assert pos == len(path), "proof length mismatch"
225	    return root
226	
227	
228	def big_root_turn_fold(record, m, n, path):
229	    """Structurally different: walk the containing interval from the root
230	    downward recording only left/right turns, then fold the path hashes
231	    leaf-to-root (deepest turn first) in a single pass."""
232	    turns = []
233	    lo, hi = 0, n
234	    while hi - lo > 1:
235	        size = hi - lo
236	        k = 1 << ((size - 1).bit_length() - 1)
237	        if m < lo + k:
238	            turns.append(True)   # accumulated hash will be the LEFT child
239	            hi = lo + k
240	        else:
241	            turns.append(False)  # accumulated hash will be the RIGHT child
242	            lo = lo + k
243	    assert len(turns) == len(path), "proof length mismatch"
244	    acc = sha256(b"\x00" + record)
245	    for i, is_left in enumerate(reversed(turns)):
246	        if is_left:
247	            acc = sha256(b"\x01" + acc + path[i])
248	        else:
249	            acc = sha256(b"\x01" + path[i] + acc)
250	    return acc
251

253	POW63 = 1 << 63

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent reference vectors for roottrace root-value regression tests.

This script is NOT the program under test and does not execute roottrace.  It
computes RFC 6962 section 2.1 SHA-256 Merkle Tree Hash roots with two
independently written algorithms over the standard library `hashlib.sha256`:

  * mth_recursive  - direct transcription of the RFC 6962 definition
                     (empty -> SHA-256(""); one leaf -> SHA-256(0x00||d);
                     n > 1 -> SHA-256(0x01 || MTH(0:k) || MTH(k:n)) with k the
                     largest power of two strictly smaller than n)
  * mth_fold       - order-sensitive left-to-right stack fold using the same
                     leaf/node prefixes (a structurally different computation
                     that must agree)

It also computes RFC 6962 section 2.1.1 inclusion (audit) paths in two
structurally different ways:

  * audit_path_recursive - direct transcription of the PATH definition
  * audit_path_fold      - the stack fold builds explicit subtree nodes with
                           intervals; the path is collected by walking from
                           the root down to the leaf's node

A recursive RFC verifier (verify_inclusion) re-hashes every printed proof and
must arrive back at the batch root; proofs for duplicate content at another
position are additionally checked NOT to verify.

A final section covers trees too large to materialise (sizes 2**63, 2**63+1
and 2**64-1): the audit path is built from deterministic synthetic sibling
hashes and the root an honest verifier must recompute is derived two
structurally different ways (recursive descent, and an iterative top-down
turn walk folded leaf-to-root), which must agree.

Records are split exactly as roottrace documents: raw bytes on LF, the
separator excluded, a trailing LF only terminates the last record, and an
empty file holds zero records.

Run:  python3 tests/reference/rfc6962_vectors.py
The printed constants are copied verbatim into tests/root_regression.rs and
tests/long_record_regression.rs.  Nothing here reads roottrace output, so the
expected roots are fixed independently of the implementation being checked.
"""

import hashlib


def sha256(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).digest()


def mth_recursive(records):
    n = len(records)
    if n == 0:
        return sha256(b"")
    if n == 1:
        return sha256(b"\x00" + records[0])
    # Largest power of two strictly smaller than n.
    k = 1 << ((n - 1).bit_length() - 1)
    return sha256(b"\x01" + mth_recursive(records[:k]) + mth_recursive(records[k:]))


def mth_fold(records):
    # Iterative, structurally independent formulation: walk leaves left to
    # right, folding completed equal-height subtrees; a trailing uneven stack
    # is combined right-to-left.  Same RFC 6962 result, order sensitive.
    def node(left, right):
        return sha256(b"\x01" + left + right)

    stack = []  # (height, hash)
    for r in records:
        h, height = sha256(b"\x00" + r), 0
        while stack and stack[-1][0] == height:
            _, lh = stack.pop()
            h, height = node(lh, h), height + 1
        stack.append((height, h))
    if not stack:
        return sha256(b"")
    root = stack[-1][1]
    for _, h in reversed(stack[:-1]):
        root = node(h, root)
    return root if stack else sha256(b"")


def split_records(data: bytes):
    if not data:
        return []
    records = data.split(b"\n")
    if data.endswith(b"\n"):
        records.pop()
    return records


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RFC 6962 section 2.1.1 inclusion (audit) paths.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def audit_path_recursive(records, m):
    """Direct transcription of the PATH definition, leaf-to-root order.

    PATH(m, [d0]) = []
    PATH(m, [d0..d(n-1)]) =
        PATH(m, d[0:k])       + [MTH(d[k:n])]   if m < k
        PATH(m - k, d[k:n])   + [MTH(d[0:k])]   if m >= k
    """
    n = len(records)
    if not 0 <= m < n:
        raise IndexError(f"index {m} out of range for {n} record(s)")
    if n == 1:
        return []
    k = 1 << ((n - 1).bit_length() - 1)
    if m < k:
        return audit_path_recursive(records[:k], m) + [mth_recursive(records[k:])]
    return audit_path_recursive(records[k:], m - k) + [mth_recursive(records[:k])]


def audit_path_fold(records, m):
    """Structurally different path producer: descend from the root to leaf m
    using the RFC split, computing each sibling subtree hash with the stack
    fold mth_fold (never mth_recursive), then reverse into leaf-to-root
    order. This shares no recursion structure with audit_path_recursive."""
    n = len(records)
    if not 0 <= m < n:
        raise IndexError(f"index {m} out of range for {n} record(s)")
    if n == 1:
        return []
    lo, hi = 0, n
    top_down = []
    while hi - lo > 1:
        size = hi - lo
        k = 1 << ((size - 1).bit_length() - 1)
        if m < lo + k:
            top_down.append(mth_fold(records[lo + k:hi]))
            hi = lo + k
        else:
            top_down.append(mth_fold(records[lo:lo + k]))
            lo = lo + k
    return list(reversed(top_down))


def verify_inclusion(leaf, m, n, path):
    """RFC 6962-bis recursive verifier: re-derive combination order from the
    tree geometry while consuming the supplied path. Returns the root."""
    def sub(mm, nn, pos):
        if nn == 1:
            return sha256(b"\x00" + leaf), pos
        k = 1 << ((nn - 1).bit_length() - 1)
        if mm < k:
            lh, pos = sub(mm, k, pos)
            rh = path[pos]
            pos += 1
        else:
            rh, pos = sub(mm - k, nn - k, pos)
            lh = path[pos]
            pos += 1
        return sha256(b"\x01" + lh + rh), pos

    root, pos = sub(m, n, 0)
    assert pos == len(path), "proof length mismatch"
    return root


def root_of_file_bytes(data: bytes):
    recs = split_records(data)
    a, b = mth_recursive(recs), mth_fold(recs)
    assert a == b, "reference algorithms disagree"
    return a.hex(), recs


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Big-tree inclusion proofs: tree sizes 2**63, 2**63+1 and 2**64-1 sit at or
# above the signed/unsigned 64-bit boundary, so no batch file can ever be
# materialised for them. The proof is therefore synthetic: one fixed target
# record, and an audit path whose element i is the deterministic 32-byte
# value written as the 64-character lowercase hex of i (reproduced in Rust
# as format!("{i:064x}")). The trusted root is whatever an honest RFC 6962
# verifier recombines from (record, leaf_index, tree_size, audit_path); it is
# derived here by two structurally different computations that must agree.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

BIG_TREE_RECORD = b"big-tree-record\x00\xff\xfe"


def big_tree_path(depth):
    return [bytes.fromhex("%064x" % i) for i in range(depth)]


def big_tree_path_for(m, n):
    """The synthetic audit path for leaf m in a tree of n records: one
    element per level on the root-to-leaf descent."""
    depth = 0
    lo, hi = 0, n
    while hi - lo > 1:
        size = hi - lo
        k = 1 << ((size - 1).bit_length() - 1)
        if m < lo + k:
            hi = lo + k
        else:
            lo = lo + k
        depth += 1
    return big_tree_path(depth)


def big_root_recursive(record, m, n, path):
    """Direct transcription of the RFC 6962-bis recursive verifier: re-derive
    the combination order from the (uneven) subtree geometry while consuming
    the path in its given leaf-to-root order."""
    leaf = sha256(b"\x00" + record)

    def sub(mm, nn, pos):
        if nn == 1:
            return leaf, pos
        k = 1 << ((nn - 1).bit_length() - 1)
        if mm < k:
            lh, pos = sub(mm, k, pos)
            rh = path[pos]
            pos += 1
        else:
            rh, pos = sub(mm - k, nn - k, pos)
            lh = path[pos]
            pos += 1
        return sha256(b"\x01" + lh + rh), pos

    root, pos = sub(m, n, 0)
    assert pos == len(path), "proof length mismatch"
    return root


def big_root_turn_fold(record, m, n, path):
    """Structurally different: walk the containing interval from the root
    downward recording only left/right turns, then fold the path hashes
    leaf-to-root (deepest turn first) in a single pass."""
    turns = []
    lo, hi = 0, n
    while hi - lo > 1:
        size = hi - lo
        k = 1 << ((size - 1).bit_length() - 1)
        if m < lo + k:
            turns.append(True)   # accumulated hash will be the LEFT child
            hi = lo + k
        else:
            turns.append(False)  # accumulated hash will be the RIGHT child
            lo = lo + k
    assert len(turns) == len(path), "proof length mismatch"
    acc = sha256(b"\x00" + record)
    for i, is_left in enumerate(reversed(turns)):
        if is_left:
            acc = sha256(b"\x01" + acc + path[i])
        else:
            acc = sha256(b"\x01" + path[i] + acc)
    return acc


POW63 = 1 << 63
U64_MAX = (1 << 64) - 1

# (tag, tree_size, leaf_index): first and last records, both sides of the
# left/right subtree boundary k (largest power of two strictly below the
# size), and indices straddling the 32-bit boundary. Every index beyond
# 2**32-1 exercises exact 64-bit index handling.
BIG_TREE_CASES = [
    ("2**63 (power-of-two tree), first record", POW63, 0),
    ("2**63, record 2**32-1 (top of 32-bit range)", POW63, (1 << 32) - 1),
    ("2**63, record 2**32 (first index past 32 bits)", POW63, 1 << 32),
    ("2**63, record k-1 (last of left subtree)", POW63, (1 << 62) - 1),
    ("2**63, record k (first of right subtree)", POW63, 1 << 62),
    ("2**63, last record", POW63, POW63 - 1),
    ("2**63+1 (uneven), first record", POW63 + 1, 0),
    ("2**63+1 (uneven), record k-1 (last of left subtree)", POW63 + 1, POW63 - 1),
    ("2**63+1 (uneven), last record = k (lone right subtree)", POW63 + 1, POW63),
    ("2**64-1 (uneven), first record", U64_MAX, 0),
    ("2**64-1 (uneven), record k-1 (last of left subtree)", U64_MAX, POW63 - 1),
    ("2**64-1 (uneven), record k (first of right subtree)", U64_MAX, POW63),
    ("2**64-1 (uneven), last record", U64_MAX, U64_MAX - 1),
]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fixed batches. The first seven records are shared by the 7/8/9 batches;
# records include duplicated content at two distinct positions (r0 == r4),
# an empty record (r3), a CR-only distinction and non-UTF-8 bytes.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# No record may contain LF: LF is the record separator, not content.
R = [
    b"alpha",                # r0
    b"beta",                 # r1
    b"",                     # r2 empty record
    b"gamma",                # r3
    b"alpha",                # r4 == r0 byte-for-byte, different position
    b"delta\r",              # r5 trailing CR is part of the content
    b"\xff\xfe\x00binary",   # r6 non-UTF-8 and NUL bytes
    b"epsilon",              # r7 eighth record, distinct content
    b"zeta\x01tail",         # r8 ninth record, distinct from r7
]

BASE7 = R[:7]
BASE8 = R[:8]
BASE9 = R[:9]

# Variant A: change ONE position of the duplicated content (r4, equal to r0)
# to other bytes.
V_DUP = list(BASE9)
assert V_DUP[4] == V_DUP[0]
V_DUP[4] = b"alpha-changed"

# Variant B: swap two records holding different content (r1 and r5).
V_SWAP = list(BASE9)
V_SWAP[1], V_SWAP[5] = V_SWAP[5], V_SWAP[1]
assert V_SWAP != BASE9

# Variant C: omit the empty record r2 (8 records, but a different sequence
# from B8 - dropping an empty record must change the root).
V_DROP_EMPTY = [r for i, r in enumerate(BASE9) if i != 2]
assert len(V_DROP_EMPTY) == 8 and V_DROP_EMPTY != BASE8

# Variant D: include one record twice - append another copy of r0 (10 records).
V_DUP_INSERT = BASE9 + [BASE9[0]]
assert len(V_DUP_INSERT) == 10


def join_lf(records, trailing=True):
    data = b"\n".join(records)
    if trailing and records:
        data += b"\n"
    return data


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Long-record batches.
#
# A leaf hashes SHA-256(0x00 || record), so record lengths 54/55/56 make the
# leaf input 55/56/57 bytes long (squeezed against the 56-byte SHA-256
# padding boundary, where the 0x80 terminator and length field spill into a
# second block), lengths 63/64/65 make it 64/65/66 bytes (exactly one block,
# then one and two bytes into a second block), and L135's leaf input is 136
# bytes (content runs into a third block). A truncating/duplicating block
# walk, or mistaking any content byte for a separator, shows up as a wrong
# fixed root.
#
# Every record carries NUL, non-UTF-8 (0xff/0xfe) and CR bytes INSIDE it and
# ends on a non-text byte (NUL, CR or non-UTF-8), so binary fidelity is
# exercised at both the interior and the tail. No record contains LF.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def make_long_record(n, tag, tail):
    # Explicit, deterministic construction (no randomness): fixed head with
    # the interior binary bytes, fixed ASCII fill, fixed tail byte.
    head = b"L" + tag + b":\x00\xff\xfe\r"
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
    rec = head
    i = 0
    while len(rec) < n - 1:
        rec += bytes([alphabet[i % len(alphabet)]])
        i += 1
    rec += bytes([tail])
    assert len(rec) == n
    assert b"\n" not in rec
    assert 0x00 in rec and 0x0D in rec and any(b >= 0x80 for b in rec)
    return rec


L54 = make_long_record(54, b"54", 0x00)    # tail byte: NUL
L55 = make_long_record(55, b"55", 0x0D)    # tail byte: CR
L56 = make_long_record(56, b"56", 0xFF)    # tail byte: non-UTF-8
L63 = make_long_record(63, b"63", 0x00)    # tail byte: NUL
L64 = make_long_record(64, b"64", 0x0D)    # tail byte: CR
L65 = make_long_record(65, b"65", 0xFE)    # tail byte: non-UTF-8
L135 = make_long_record(135, b"135", 0xFF)  # 135 > 128, tail byte non-UTF-8

# Exactly ONE byte changed - the final byte - of the same long record. The
# fixed root must correspond to the whole MODIFIED record; an implementation
# that only processes the front part cannot tell these apart.
L65_M = L65[:-1] + b"Z"
L135_M = L135[:-1] + b"~"
assert len(L65_M) == len(L65) and L65_M[:-1] == L65[:-1] and L65_M[-1] != L65[-1]
assert len(L135_M) == len(L135) and L135_M[:-1] == L135[:-1] and L135_M[-1] != L135[-1]

# (Rust constant name, record) for every single-record long batch.
SINGLE_LONG = [
    ("L54", L54), ("L55", L55), ("L56", L56),
    ("L63", L63), ("L64", L64), ("L65", L65),
    ("L135", L135),
    ("L65_M", L65_M), ("L135_M", L135_M),
]
assert [len(r) for _, r in SINGLE_LONG[:6]] == [54, 55, 56, 63, 64, 65]
assert len(L135) > 128

# One fixed batch of long AND short records (10 records, so the RFC 6962
# subtree split k=8 puts long records on both sides: L54/L63/L135 in the
# left subtree, L65 in the right subtree). It also contains an empty record
# and a short record with binary bytes.
MIXED = [
    b"alpha",          # 0 short
    b"",               # 1 empty record
    L54,               # 2 long (54)
    b"beta\r",         # 3 short, trailing CR
    L63,               # 4 long (63)
    b"\xff\x00z",      # 5 short with non-UTF-8 and NUL
    L135,              # 6 long (>128)
    b"middle",         # 7 short
    L65,               # 8 long (65), right subtree
    b"end-record\x01", # 9 short, right subtree
]
assert len(MIXED) == 10
# Same mixed batch with only the final byte of the L65 record (position 8)
# changed: long records inside a batch must follow the same byte-exact rule
# as single-record batches.
MIXED_M = list(MIXED)
MIXED_M[8] = L65_M


BATCHES = [
    ("B7", join_lf(BASE7), "seven shared records", True),
    ("B8", join_lf(BASE8), "seven shared records + eighth (epsilon)", True),
    ("B9", join_lf(BASE9), "seven shared records + eighth + ninth (zeta...)", True),
    ("V_DUP", join_lf(V_DUP), "B9 with duplicate position r4 changed to other bytes", True),
    ("V_SWAP", join_lf(V_SWAP), "B9 with r1 and r5 (different content) swapped", True),
    ("V_DROP_EMPTY", join_lf(V_DROP_EMPTY), "B9 with the empty record r2 omitted (8 records, != B8)", True),
    ("V_DUP_INSERT", join_lf(V_DUP_INSERT), "B9 plus one extra duplicate of r0 (10 records)", True),
    ("EMPTY", b"", "empty file: zero records", False),
    ("ONE_LF", b"\n", "single LF: one empty record", False),
]

# Single-record long batches, each written with and without a trailing LF.
for name, rec in SINGLE_LONG:
    BATCHES.append(
        (name, join_lf([rec]), f"one long record of {len(rec)} bytes "
         f"(leaf input {1 + len(rec)} bytes)", True)
    )

# Fixed mixed batch of long and short records, plus its one-tail-byte variant.
BATCHES += [
    ("MIXED", join_lf(MIXED),
     "fixed batch of 10 long and short records (long records in both k=8 subtrees)", True),
    ("MIXED_M", join_lf(MIXED_M),
     "MIXED with only the final byte of the L65 record changed", True),
]


def rust_byte_string(data: bytes) -> str:
    out = "b\""
    for byte in data:
        if byte == 0x0A:
            out += "\\n"
        elif byte == 0x0D:
            out += "\\r"
        elif byte == 0x00:
            out += "\\x00"
        elif byte == 0x01:
            out += "\\x01"
        elif byte == 0x22:
            out += "\\\""
        elif byte == 0x5C:
            out += "\\\\"
        elif 0x20 <= byte < 0x7F:
            out += chr(byte)
        else:
            out += "\\x%02x" % byte
    return out + "\""


def main():
    print("# Generated by tests/reference/rfc6962_vectors.py")
    print("# Two independent RFC 6962 implementations agree for every vector.")
    print()
    labels = []
    for name, data, desc, trailing in BATCHES:
        digest, recs = root_of_file_bytes(data)
        labels.append((name, digest))
        print(f"# {name}: {desc}")
        print(f"#   {len(recs)} record(s): {[r for r in recs]!r}")
        print(f"#   file bytes ({len(data)}): {data!r}")
        print(f"#   MTH = {digest}")
        print()

    print("# Rust constants (paste into tests/root_regression.rs or")
    print("# tests/long_record_regression.rs):")
    for name, digest in labels:
        print(f"const ROOT_{name}: &str = \"{digest}\";")
    print()

    # Trailing-LF equivalence check for every nonempty batch.
    print("# trailing LF equivalence (same root with and without final LF):")
    equiv = [(BASE7, "B7"), (BASE8, "B8"), (BASE9, "B9"),
             (V_DUP, "V_DUP"), (V_SWAP, "V_SWAP"),
             (V_DROP_EMPTY, "V_DROP_EMPTY"),
             (V_DUP_INSERT, "V_DUP_INSERT"),
             (MIXED, "MIXED"), (MIXED_M, "MIXED_M")]
    equiv += [([rec], name) for name, rec in SINGLE_LONG]
    for recs, tag in equiv:
        a, _ = root_of_file_bytes(join_lf(recs, trailing=True))
        b, _ = root_of_file_bytes(join_lf(recs, trailing=False))
        assert a == b
        print(f"#   {tag}: {a}")
    print()

    # Sanity assertions that the variants really differ and that order matters.
    roots = {name: digest for name, digest in labels}
    assert roots["B8"] != roots["B7"]
    assert roots["B9"] != roots["B8"]
    assert roots["V_DUP"] != roots["B9"]
    assert roots["V_SWAP"] != roots["B9"]
    assert roots["V_DROP_EMPTY"] != roots["B9"]
    assert roots["V_DROP_EMPTY"] != roots["B8"]
    assert roots["V_DUP_INSERT"] != roots["B9"]
    assert roots["EMPTY"] != roots["ONE_LF"]
    assert roots["EMPTY"] == "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"

    # Long-record sanity: every boundary length has its own root, the tail-byte
    # variants differ from their originals (and from one another), and the
    # mixed batch differs from every single-record batch and its variant.
    for name, _ in SINGLE_LONG:
        assert all(roots[name] != roots[other]
                   for other, _ in SINGLE_LONG if other != name), name
    assert roots["L65_M"] != roots["L65"]
    assert roots["L135_M"] != roots["L135"]
    assert roots["MIXED"] != roots["MIXED_M"]
    for name, _ in SINGLE_LONG:
        assert roots["MIXED"] != roots[name]
        assert roots["MIXED_M"] != roots[name]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Inclusion proofs: the two structurally different path producers must
    # agree at every position of every fixed sequence, and each path must
    # verify back to the batch root via the recursive verifier.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    proof_sequences = [
        ("B7", BASE7), ("B8", BASE8), ("B9", BASE9),
        ("V_DUP", V_DUP), ("V_SWAP", V_SWAP),
        ("V_DROP_EMPTY", V_DROP_EMPTY), ("V_DUP_INSERT", V_DUP_INSERT),
        ("MIXED", MIXED), ("MIXED_M", MIXED_M),
        ("ONE_LF", [b""]),
    ] + [(name, [rec]) for name, rec in SINGLE_LONG]

    for tag, recs in proof_sequences:
        root = bytes.fromhex(roots[tag])
        n = len(recs)
        for m in range(n):
            p1 = audit_path_recursive(recs, m)
            p2 = audit_path_fold(recs, m)
            assert p1 == p2, f"path producers disagree for {tag} m={m}"
            got = verify_inclusion(recs[m], m, n, p1)
            assert got == root, f"proof does not verify for {tag} m={m}"
            # Every element is a 32-byte node hash; the single-record path
            # is empty.
            assert all(isinstance(h, bytes) and len(h) == 32 for h in p1)
        if n == 1:
            assert audit_path_recursive(recs, 0) == []

    # Duplicate content at positions 0 and 4 of BASE9: the proof for one
    # position must NOT verify the same bytes at the other position.
    p_dup_0 = audit_path_recursive(BASE9, 0)
    p_dup_4 = audit_path_recursive(BASE9, 4)
    assert p_dup_0 != p_dup_4
    assert verify_inclusion(BASE9[4], 0, 9, p_dup_4) != mth_recursive(BASE9)
    assert verify_inclusion(BASE9[0], 4, 9, p_dup_0) != mth_recursive(BASE9)

    # Fixed proof vectors emitted for the Rust prove regression tests:
    # B9 (uneven, n=9) at its first, duplicate-content and last positions;
    # B8 (balanced) mid-tree; and a single empty record (empty path).
    def emit_proof(const_tag, seq_name, recs, m):
        root = mth_recursive(recs)
        path = audit_path_recursive(recs, m)
        print(f"# Inclusion proof for {seq_name} (n={len(recs)}) at m={m}; "
              f"two independent path producers agree and the path verifies.")
        print(f"const PROOF_{const_tag}_TREE_SIZE: u64 = {len(recs)};")
        print(f"const PROOF_{const_tag}_LEAF_INDEX: u64 = {m};")
        print(f"const PROOF_{const_tag}_ROOT: &str = \"{root.hex()}\";")
        elems = ", ".join(f"\"{h.hex()}\"" for h in path)
        print(f"const PROOF_{const_tag}_AUDIT_PATH: &[&str] = &[{elems}];")
        print()

    print("# Fixed inclusion-proof vectors (RFC 6962 section 2.1.1,")
    print("# leaf-to-root order; hashes are lowercase hex):")
    print()
    emit_proof("B9_M0", "BASE9", BASE9, 0)
    emit_proof("B9_M4", "BASE9 (duplicate 'alpha' position)", BASE9, 4)
    emit_proof("B9_M8", "BASE9 (last record, uneven right subtree)", BASE9, 8)
    emit_proof("B8_M3", "BASE8 (balanced 8-record tree)", BASE8, 3)
    emit_proof("MIXED_M8", "MIXED (long record L65 in the k=8 right subtree)", MIXED, 8)
    emit_proof("ONE_LF_M0", "single LF (one empty record)", [b""], 0)

    # Payload literal used by the Rust tests to materialise the batches.
    print("# Rust file payloads:")
    for name, data, desc, trailing in BATCHES:
        print(f"# {name} {desc}")
        print(f"const PAYLOAD_{name}: &[u8] = {rust_byte_string(data)};")
    print()
    # Trailing-LF variants of the three base batches.
    for recs, tag in [(BASE7, "B7"), (BASE8, "B8"), (BASE9, "B9")]:
        print(f"const PAYLOAD_{tag}_NOTRAIL: &[u8] = "
              f"{rust_byte_string(join_lf(recs, trailing=False))};")
    print()

    # Long-record byte literals (records, not file payloads) and the fixed
    # long/short mixed batches as record-slice constants.
    print("# Rust long-record literals (raw record bytes, no separators):")
    for name, rec in SINGLE_LONG:
        print(f"# {name}: {len(rec)}-byte record, root ROOT_{name} = {roots[name]}")
        print(f"const REC_{name}: &[u8] = {rust_byte_string(rec)};")
    print()
    print("# Fixed mixed batches as record sequences:")
    single_by_value = {rec: name for name, rec in SINGLE_LONG}

    def rust_record_list(records, const_name):
        print(f"const {const_name}: &[&[u8]] = &[")
        for rec in records:
            if rec in single_by_value:
                print(f"    REC_{single_by_value[rec]},")
            else:
                print(f"    {rust_byte_string(rec)},")
        print("];")

    rust_record_list(MIXED, "MIXED_RECORDS")
    print(f"#   root ROOT_MIXED = {roots['MIXED']}")
    rust_record_list(MIXED_M, "MIXED_M_RECORDS")
    print(f"#   root ROOT_MIXED_M = {roots['MIXED_M']}")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Big-tree synthetic proofs. First anchor the two big-tree root
    # computations to the already cross-validated small-tree machinery:
    # on every real batch they must recompute the batch root from the real
    # audit path, exactly like verify_inclusion.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for tag, recs in proof_sequences:
        n = len(recs)
        expected = bytes.fromhex(roots[tag])
        for m in range(n):
            path = audit_path_recursive(recs, m)
            assert big_root_recursive(recs[m], m, n, path) == expected

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent reference vectors for the MULTI-READ root regression tests.

This script is NOT the program under test and does not execute roottrace.  It
computes the expected RFC 6962 section 2.1 SHA-256 Merkle Tree Hash roots for
a batch whose file is large enough that `roottrace root` (which streams the
file through a fixed 64 KiB read buffer) cannot see any whole record in one
read: one record is 140000 bytes (> 128 KiB) and spans several reads, and two
record-separating LFs land exactly on the last/first byte of a read boundary.

The roots are computed with the two structurally different, already
cross-validated reference algorithms from rfc6962_vectors.py (the RFC's
recursive definition and an order-sensitive stack fold over the standard
library `hashlib.sha256`); they must agree.  The Rust test
tests/multi_read_regression.rs rebuilds the exact same bytes with the same
deterministic construction and pins the printed constants, so the expected
roots are fixed independently of the implementation being checked.

Batch record sequence (10 records, a non-power-of-two count; RFC 6962 splits
k=8, so the long record at position 4 sits in the left subtree and the
trailing short record at position 9 in the right one):

    0  b"alpha"              short; duplicated byte-for-byte at position 6
    1  b""                   empty record
    2  PAD                   65528 bytes: b"pad:" + b"p" * 65524, placed so
                             its terminating LF is the LAST byte of the first
                             64 KiB read (file offset 65535)
    3  b""                   empty record; its LF is the FIRST byte of the
                             second read (offset 65536), so two consecutive
                             LFs straddle the read boundary
    4  LONG                  140000 bytes (> 128 KiB), spanning reads; NUL,
                             CR and non-UTF-8 bytes in both halves and at the
                             tail; distinct head/mid/tail markers
    5  b"beta\\r"            short, trailing CR is content
    6  b"alpha"              duplicate of position 0 (must not be merged)
    7  b""                   empty record
    8  b"\\xff\\x00z"        short, non-UTF-8 and NUL bytes
    9  b"end-record\\x01"    trailing short record, must reach the final root

Run:  python3 tests/reference/rfc6962_multiread_vectors.py
"""

import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from rfc6962_vectors import mth_fold, mth_recursive, split_records

READ_BUF = 64 * 1024  # the fixed read buffer `roottrace root` streams through

LONG_LEN = 140_000  # > 128 KiB: the record spans several consecutive reads
# Bytes before PAD: b"alpha\n" (6) + b"\n" (1) = 7.  PAD's terminating LF must
# land at offset READ_BUF - 1 (the last byte the first read returns).
PAD_LEN = READ_BUF - 1 - 7  # 65528
# Position of the single changed content byte inside LONG: in the second half
# of the record and (as a file offset) inside a later read than the record's
# first bytes.
MOD_POS = 100_000


def fill_byte(i: int) -> int:
    """Deterministic pseudo-random content byte; LF is remapped so the long
    record never contains its own separator.  Identical to the Rust
    `fill_byte` in tests/multi_read_regression.rs."""
    b = ((i * 2654435761) & 0xFFFFFFFF) >> 13 & 0xFF
    return 0x0B if b == 0x0A else b


def long_record() -> bytes:
    rec = bytearray(fill_byte(i) for i in range(LONG_LEN))
    rec[0:13] = b"MREAD\x00\xff\xfe\rHEAD"          # first-half marker
    mid = LONG_LEN // 2
    marker = b"\x00\xff\rSECOND-HALF"               # second-half marker
    rec[mid:mid + len(marker)] = marker
    tail = b"\x00TAIL\r\xff"                        # tail marker, non-text end
    rec[LONG_LEN - len(tail):] = tail
    return bytes(rec)


def long_record_m() -> bytes:
    """The same record with exactly ONE non-LF content byte changed, at
    MOD_POS in the second half; record length and every other byte kept."""
    rec = bytearray(LONG)
    old = rec[MOD_POS]
    rec[MOD_POS] = 0x41 if old != 0x41 else 0x42  # 'A' or 'B', never LF
    assert rec[MOD_POS] != old
    return bytes(rec)


PAD = b"pad:" + b"p" * (PAD_LEN - 4)
LONG = long_record()
LONG_M = long_record_m()

RECORDS = [
    b"alpha",
    b"",
    PAD,
    b"",
    LONG,
    b"beta\r",
    b"alpha",
    b"",
    b"\xff\x00z",
    b"end-record\x01",
]
RECORDS_M = [
    b"alpha",
    b"",
    PAD,
    b"",
    LONG_M,
    b"beta\r",
    b"alpha",
    b"",
    b"\xff\x00z",
    b"end-record\x01",
]


def join_lf(records, trailing=True):
    data = b"\n".join(records)
    if trailing and records:
        data += b"\n"
    return data


def root_of(records):
    a, b = mth_recursive(records), mth_fold(records)
    assert a == b, "reference algorithms disagree"
    return a.hex()


def describe(records):
    out = []
    for i, r in enumerate(records):
        if len(r) <= 32:
            out.append(f"    {i}: {len(r)} byte(s) {r!r}")
        else:
            out.append(f"    {i}: {len(r)} byte(s) {r[:16]!r} ... {r[-8:]!r}")
    return "\n".join(out)


def main():
    n = len(RECORDS)
    assert n == 10 and n & (n - 1) != 0, "record count must be a non-power of two"
    assert RECORDS[0] == RECORDS[6], "duplicate content at positions 0 and 6"
    assert RECORDS[1] == RECORDS[3] == RECORDS[7] == b"", "empty records"

    # Long-record shape: > 128 KiB, no LF anywhere, NUL/CR/non-UTF-8 in both
    # halves and at the tail, distinct markers in each region.
    half = LONG_LEN // 2
    assert LONG_LEN > 128 * 1024
    assert b"\n" not in LONG
    for region in (LONG[:half], LONG[half:]):
        assert 0x00 in region and 0x0D in region
        assert any(b >= 0x80 for b in region)
    assert LONG[:13] == b"MREAD\x00\xff\xfe\rHEAD"
    assert LONG[half:half + 14] == b"\x00\xff\rSECOND-HALF"
    assert LONG[-7:] == b"\x00TAIL\r\xff"

    # The one-byte modification: second half, non-LF, everything else equal.
    assert MOD_POS > half
    assert LONG_M != LONG and len(LONG_M) == len(LONG)
    diffs = [i for i in range(LONG_LEN) if LONG[i] != LONG_M[i]]
    assert diffs == [MOD_POS] and LONG_M[MOD_POS] != 0x0A

    # File layout: LFs at offsets 65535/65536 are consecutive and straddle
    # the 64 KiB read boundary; the long record spans several reads.
    data = join_lf(RECORDS)
    assert data[65535] == 0x0A and data[65536] == 0x0A
    assert data[65534] != 0x0A and data[65537] != 0x0A
    long_start = 7 + PAD_LEN + 1 + 1  # after PAD's LF and the empty record's LF
    long_end = long_start + LONG_LEN - 1
    assert long_start // READ_BUF < long_end // READ_BUF
    assert long_end // READ_BUF - long_start // READ_BUF >= 2, "must span >= 3 reads"
    assert split_records(data) == RECORDS
    assert split_records(join_lf(RECORDS, trailing=False)) == RECORDS

    root = root_of(RECORDS)
    root_m = root_of(RECORDS_M)
    assert root != root_m, "one content byte in the second half must matter"
    # Trailing-LF equivalence: both file forms encode the same sequence.
    assert split_records(data) == split_records(join_lf(RECORDS, trailing=False))

    print("# Generated by tests/reference/rfc6962_multiread_vectors.py")
    print("# Two independent RFC 6962 implementations agree for every vector.")
    print("#")
    print("# MREAD batch record sequence (10 records, non-power-of-two):")
    print(describe(RECORDS))
    print("#")
    print("# MREAD_M: identical except LONG[100000] changed")
    print(f"#   {LONG[MOD_POS]:#04x} -> {LONG_M[MOD_POS]:#04x} (second half of the long record)")
    print("#")
    print(f"# file bytes: {len(data)} (with trailing LF), "
          f"read buffer {READ_BUF}; long record at file offsets "
          f"{long_start}..{long_end} (reads {long_start // READ_BUF}..{long_end // READ_BUF});")
    print("# record-separating LFs at offsets 65535 and 65536 straddle the "
          "first read boundary")
    print()
    print(f"const ROOT_MREAD: &str = \"{root}\";")
    print(f"const ROOT_MREAD_M: &str = \"{root_m}\";")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent reference vectors for the MULTI-READ root regression tests.

This script is NOT the program under test and does not execute roottrace.  It
computes the expected RFC 6962 section 2.1 SHA-256 Merkle Tree Hash roots for
a batch whose file is large enough that `roottrace root` (which streams the
file through a fixed 64 KiB read buffer) cannot see any whole record in one
read: one record is 140000 bytes (> 128 KiB) and spans several reads, and two
record-separating LFs land exactly on the last/first byte of a read boundary.

The roots are computed with the two structurally different, already
cross-validated reference algorithms from rfc6962_vectors.py (the RFC's
recursive definition and an order-sensitive stack fold over the standard
library `hashlib.sha256`); they must agree.  Inclusion (audit) paths for the
long record (position 4) and the trailing short record (position 9) - in both
the original and the one-byte-modified batch - are likewise produced by the
two structurally different path builders from rfc6962_vectors.py (the
recursive PATH transcription and the top-down descent whose sibling hashes
come from the stack fold), must agree, and are re-hashed back to the batch
root by the independent recursive inclusion verifier; every other position of
both batches is checked the same way before the constants are printed.  The
Rust tests tests/multi_read_regression.rs and
tests/prove_multi_read_regression.rs rebuild the exact same bytes with the
same deterministic construction and pin the printed constants, so the
expected roots and audit paths are fixed independently of the implementation
being checked.

Batch record sequence (10 records, a non-power-of-two count; RFC 6962 splits
k=8, so the long record at position 4 sits in the left subtree and the
trailing short record at position 9 in the right one):

    0  b"alpha"              short; duplicated byte-for-byte at position 6
    1  b""                   empty record
    2  PAD                   65528 bytes: b"pad:" + b"p" * 65524, placed so
                             its terminating LF is the LAST byte of the first
                             64 KiB read (file offset 65535)
    3  b""                   empty record; its LF is the FIRST byte of the
                             second read (offset 65536), so two consecutive
                             LFs straddle the read boundary
    4  LONG                  140000 bytes (> 128 KiB), spanning reads; NUL,
                             CR and non-UTF-8 bytes in both halves and at the
                             tail; distinct head/mid/tail markers
    5  b"beta\\r"            short, trailing CR is content
    6  b"alpha"              duplicate of position 0 (must not be merged)
    7  b""                   empty record
    8  b"\\xff\\x00z"        short, non-UTF-8 and NUL bytes
    9  b"end-record\\x01"    trailing short record, must reach the final root

Run:  python3 tests/reference/rfc6962_multiread_vectors.py

import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from rfc6962_vectors import (
    audit_path_fold,
    audit_path_recursive,
    mth_fold,
    mth_recursive,
    split_records,
    verify_inclusion,
)

    b"",
    PAD,

    b"",

    b"end-record\x01",
]

    b"alpha",
    b"",

    b"",
    LONG_M,

    b"alpha",
    b"",
    b"\xff\x00z",
    b"end-record\x01",

    assert LONG[half:half + 14] == b"\x00\xff\rSECOND-HALF"
    assert LONG[-7:] == b"\x00TAIL\r\xff"

    # The one-byte modification: second half, non-LF, everything else equal.
    assert MOD_POS > half
    assert LONG_M != LONG and len(LONG_M) == len(LONG)
    diffs = [i for i in range(LONG_LEN) if LONG[i] != LONG_M[i]]
    assert diffs == [MOD_POS] and LONG_M[MOD_POS] != 0x0A

    # File layout: LFs at offsets 65535/65536 are consecutive and straddle
    # the 64 KiB read boundary; the long record spans several reads.
    data = join_lf(RECORDS)
    assert data[65535] == 0x0A and data[65536] == 0x0A
    assert data[65534] != 0x0A and data[65537] != 0x0A
    long_start = 7 + PAD_LEN + 1 + 1  # after PAD's LF and the empty record's LF
    long_end = long_start + LONG_LEN - 1
    assert long_start // READ_BUF < long_end // READ_BUF

    assert split_records(data) == RECORDS

    root = root_of(RECORDS)
    root_m = root_of(RECORDS_M)
    assert root != root_m, "one content byte in the second half must matter"
    # Trailing-LF equivalence: both file forms encode the same sequence.
    assert split_records(data) == split_records(join_lf(RECORDS, trailing=False))

    print("# Generated by tests/reference/rfc6962_multiread_vectors.py")
    print("# Two independent RFC 6962 implementations agree for every vector.")
    print("#")
    print("# MREAD batch record sequence (10 records, non-power-of-two):")
    print(describe(RECORDS))
    print("#")
    print("# MREAD_M: identical except LONG[100000] changed")
    print(f"#   {LONG[MOD_POS]:#04x} -> {LONG_M[MOD_POS]:#04x} (second half of the long record)")
    print("#")
    print(f"# file bytes: {len(data)} (with trailing LF), "
          f"read buffer {READ_BUF}; long record at file offsets "
          f"{long_start}..{long_end} (reads {long_start // READ_BUF}..{long_end // READ_BUF});")
    print("# record-separating LFs at offsets 65535 and 65536 straddle the "

    print()

    print(f"const ROOT_MREAD_M: &str = \"{root_m}\";")

完成。长记录批次的成员证明回归保障已补齐，全部 14 个测试目标（含新增 5 个测试）通过，无警告。

## 改动内容

**`tests/reference/rfc6962_multiread_vectors.py`**（独立正确性依据）
- 复用 `rfc6962_vectors.py` 中两种结构不同的 RFC 6962 第 2.1.1 节路径算法（递归 PATH 定义 + 自顶向下下降/栈折叠兄弟哈希），对原批次和修改批次**全部 10 个位置**互验一致，并由独立的递归包含验证器把每条路径重新哈希回批次根值后，才输出固定常量。
- 新增断言：长记录（序号 4）的路径为 4 个元素且在修改前后逐字节相同（改动在叶子内部，兄弟子树未变）；末条（序号 9）路径为 2 个元素（不均匀树形，不复制不补空），修改后首元素（记录 8 的叶子哈希）不变、次元素（覆盖长记录的左子树哈希）必变。
- 输出 `PATH_MREAD_M4`、`PATH_MREAD_M9`、`PATH_MREAD_MOD_M4`、`PATH_MREAD_MOD_M9` 四组常量；根值常量不变。

**`tests/prove_multi_read_regression.rs`**（新增，5 个测试）
- `prove` 对序号 4（140000 字节长记录）和序号 9（末条短记录）的输出逐字节等于固定 JSON 向量：`tree_size` 10、位置正确、根值与完整批次一致、路径绑定该位置；退出 0、stderr 为空、恰为一行 JSON 加换行。
- 批次文件末尾有/无 LF 对同一位置生成逐字节相同的证明（不多出空记录）。
- 两份真实 `prove` 输出交给 `verify`，配合记录原始字节（长记录原样写入、无分隔 LF、二进制字节不修剪）和独立可信值（10, ROOT_MREAD），输出恰为 `verified\n`。
- 后半段改一个非 LF 字节后：证明绑定 `ROOT_MREAD_M`；长记录路径保持原值，末条路径中覆盖长记录的子树哈希改变；修改后的证明配合新记录和新根值核验成功。
- 原长记录证明 + 修改后记录 + 原可信值：退出 1、标准输出为空、stderr 含 "verification failed" 且不含 "invalid proof"（错误分类保持核验失败）。

**`README.md`**：新增该测试文件的说明段落，并更新参考脚本段落以反映审计路径也由独立脚本固定。

现有命令、证明格式和错误分类均未改动（`src/` 无修改）。

lastPrompt: 为 roottrace 的成员证明生成功能补充长记录批次的回归保障。现有的大记录批次已经校验根值，也确认末条记录能够生成证明，但还没有完整约束这类批次的审计路径及实际核验结果。本次围绕一份十条记录的批次展开：序号 4 是一条 140000 字节的记录，内部及末尾含 NUL、CR 和非 UTF-8 字节，批次中仍有短记录、空记录和重复内容。长记录只占一个位置，全部字节参与证明，不能被截断、拆分或跳过…
